title: Temperature-Controlled DNA Extraction from Ancient Bones
author: Elena Essel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bje5kjg6
materials: Sodium-phosphate buffer (0.5 M sodium phosphate, pH 7.0, 0.1 % Tween 20) is prepared by combining the following reagents: 49.5 mL Sodium phosphate solution, 0.5 M, pH 7.0 Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #J60158.AP 50 µL TWEEN® 20 Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #T2700-100ML (CAS: 9005-64-5)

Tris-Tween wash buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 0.1% Tween-20) is prepared by combining the following reagents: 49.5 mL Water for HPLC Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #270733 (CAS: 7732-18-5) 0.5 mL Tris buffer pH 8.0 (1 M) for molecular biology AppliChem Catalog #A4577,0500 50 µL TWEEN® 20 Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #T2700-100ML (CAS: 9005-64-5)

Lysis buffer (0.45 M EDTA, pH 8.0, 0.05% Tween-20 and 0.25 mg/ml proteinase K) is prepared by combining the following reagents: 3.725 mL Water for HPLC Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #270733 (CAS: 7732-18-5) 45 mL EDTA solution pH 8.0 (0.5 M) for molecular biology AppliChem Catalog #A4892,1000 25 µL TWEEN® 20 Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #T2700-100ML (CAS: 9005-64-5) 1.25 mL 10 mg/ml proteinase K solution in water (prepared from Proteinase K 100 mg Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #3115879001 ) Proteinase K is added after UV irradiation
All buffers are irradiated with UV-C light at a dose of 7 kJ/cm 2 using a cross-linker.

Thaw the sodium phosphate fractions (and lysates if necessary) at 37 °C in a thermo block with gentle shaking. Make sure the liquid is fully thawed and any crystals have completely dissolved. If desired, DNA extraction can also be performed on the Tris-Tween buffer, but DNA yields are expected to be extremely low.

steps.title: Collect bone powder
steps.instruction: In the ancient DNA cleanroom, use a sterile dentist drill to remove ~50 mg bone powder from each specimen and transfer it into a 2.0 mL DNA LoBind tube.

steps.title: Add ceramic beads
steps.instruction: Add 3–4 ceramic beads (2.8 mm, VWR International Catalog #432‑0292) to the tube to aid resuspension.

steps.title: Add sodium phosphate buffer
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL sodium phosphate buffer and vortex thoroughly to resuspend the powder.

steps.title: Temperature‑controlled phosphate washes
steps.instruction: Perform six incubations: 37 °C, 60 °C, and 90 °C each twice. For each incubation, place the tube in a thermoblock shaking at 900 rpm for 15 min. Include at least one negative‑control tube (no sample) that follows the same schedule. For the 90 °C step ensure the liquid reaches 90 °C by the end; increase block temperature if needed.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: After each incubation, centrifuge the tube for 2 min at maximum speed (≈16,400 g/13,200 rpm). Carefully pipette the supernatant into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube (pipette slowly because of beads) and store at –20 °C until DNA extraction.

steps.title: Room‑temperature Tris‑Tween wash
steps.instruction: After the final 90 °C incubation, add 1 mL Tris‑Tween buffer, vortex to resuspend, centrifuge 2 min at max speed, and transfer the supernatant to a LoBind tube; store at –20 °C or proceed to extraction.

steps.title: Lysis overnight
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL lysis buffer to the remaining pellet, vortex, wrap the tube with parafilm, and incubate with rotation at 37 °C for 8–16 h.

steps.title: Purify DNA extracts
steps.instruction: Purify 100 µL of each sodium‑phosphate supernatant and 500 µL of the final lysate using binding buffer ‘G’ as described in Glocke & Meyer (2017). Elute all extracts to a final volume of 50 µL.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Use 20 % of each DNA extract as input and prepare single‑strand libraries following Gansauge et al. (2020), including quantification and indexing.

steps.title: Trim adapters and merge reads
steps.instruction: Run leeHom to trim adapters and merge overlapping paired‑end reads into single‑molecule sequences.

steps.title: Shallow shotgun sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the libraries on an Illumina MiSeq or HiSeq2500 (or equivalent) using a paired‑end double‑index configuration (2 × 76 + 2 × 7 cycles).

steps.title: Align reads to reference
steps.instruction: Align merged reads to the chosen reference genome with BWA using ancient‑DNA parameters ‘-n 0.01 –o 2 –l 16500’.

steps.title: Filter short sequences
steps.instruction: Retain only aligned sequences that are ≥35 bp in length.

steps.title: Remove duplicate reads
steps.instruction: Merge reads sharing identical start and end coordinates into a consensus using bam‑rmdup.

description: Generate summary statistics using samtools and choose the library with the highest proportion of endogenous DNA for further sequencing. Prepare additional libraries from remaining DNA extract if necessary. The Sequence Alignment/Map format and SAMtools.. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England).
